summary: Eau Claire County, WI: 100-foot Conservation Department tower built in 1952 next to the Town of Seymour shale pit; vandalized in 1958; listed as gone.

facts.status_note: Statewide lookout list marks it Gone; the sources read give no removal date or method

staffing.status: fire spotters to man it in season; towerman Vernon Jacobson named in August 1952

events.note: Constructed at a cost of about $3,500 next to the Town of Seymour shale pit; reported July 15, 1952
Fires in an area recently added to fire protection district 10 were to be spotted from the tower; towerman Vernon Jacobson named in an August 15, 1952 item
Vandalized in late March 1958: 12 windows broken, fire-spotting protractor smashed, radio and electric heater stolen; conservation wardens and sheriff's department investigated

notes_for_editor: The 1952 article says the tower was 'about eight miles east of here'; the page has no dateline naming Eau Claire, so the story gives no distance. Brief height 30.5 m and agency match the sources. Two WebSearch calls found no removal date or cause, so the story says nothing about how it ended beyond the index status and the 1958 vandalism. Per-tower firelookout page not available (404).
